slides.title: Nurse-Client Relationship
text: Nurse-Client Relationship

You have been asked by the nurse manager to prepare a 30 minute in-service for staff about the phases of the therapeutic relationship. You were given an outline of required topics which include: Peplau’s 3 phases, cultural-competence, and working with special populations.
What are the key points to discuss with staff about Peplau’s phases?
What can nurses do to ensure they are delivering culturally competent care?
Why is this important when working with populations such as homeless individuals or individuals who may have different life preferences such as LGBTQ persons?

clients’ Rights & Types of Admission

slides.title: A 54-year-old female client is hospitalized as she is suffering from generalized anxiety disorder that is interfering with her ability to function in her daily life. Her provider just informed her that the treatment team is developing a care plan that includes medication and education regarding coping skills/lifestyle modifications. You have been assigned this client several times and you know she tends to ask a lot of questions.  As her nurse, you want to be fully prepared to help her with her new treatment plan.
text: A 54-year-old female client is hospitalized as she is suffering from generalized anxiety disorder that is interfering with her ability to function in her daily life. Her provider just informed her that the treatment team is developing a care plan that includes medication and education regarding coping skills/lifestyle modifications. You have been assigned this client several times and you know she tends to ask a lot of questions.  As her nurse, you want to be fully prepared to help her with her new treatment plan.
Identify a possible medication for anxiety disorder and what client information (side effects and client education) will you need to give the client.
What are appropriate coping mechanisms/lifestyle modifications for this client’s anxiety? Why are the skills helpful for her disorder?
What other nursing interventions are appropriate for anxiety?
Anxiety

slides.title: A 31-year-old male client is at the clinic for his outpatient appointment. He says to the nurse “my friend told me that my OCD is because I have high anxiety, but I thought it was because I have an obsession with cleanliness. Which is it?”
text: A 31-year-old male client is at the clinic for his outpatient appointment. He says to the nurse “my friend told me that my OCD is because I have high anxiety, but I thought it was because I have an obsession with cleanliness. Which is it?”
What is the best response from the nurse?
What treatment options will you expect for this client?
Should you discourage the client from excessive handwashing?
Anxiety/OCD

slides.title: Mary is a 35-year-old divorced female whose sister died six months ago after a long battle with breast cancer. Mary has been admitted to the unit for increased thoughts of hopelessness and depression. Mary seems very down and does not make much eye contact when speaking. She rarely engages in group activities on the unit and today, she gave her favorite book to another client. Mary’s journal has statements written in it like “no one will ever love me” and “I have no friends left”.
text: Mary is a 35-year-old divorced female whose sister died six months ago after a long battle with breast cancer. Mary has been admitted to the unit for increased thoughts of hopelessness and depression. Mary seems very down and does not make much eye contact when speaking. She rarely engages in group activities on the unit and today, she gave her favorite book to another client. Mary’s journal has statements written in it like “no one will ever love me” and “I have no friends left”.
What are some warning signs that indicate Mary is considering suicide?
Provide 2 statements that would be appropriate for the nurse to say to Mary and explain why each statement is appropriate.
What nursing interventions are appropriate for a person who is at risk for suicidal ideations?
Suicidal Ideation/Depression

slides.title: Two clients are admitted on the unit at almost the same time, both with electrolyte imbalance. client 1 is a 20-year-old female with average weight, callouses on her hands, and a history of shoplifting. She is impulsive and appears a little anxious. client 2 is a 19-year-old female who is underweight, reports losing 18 pounds in the last month, and she is very pale.  A new nurse asks you what the diagnosis is for each of the clients being admitted. You advise that one client is suffering from bulimia and the other is suffering from anorexia.
text: Two clients are admitted on the unit at almost the same time, both with electrolyte imbalance. client 1 is a 20-year-old female with average weight, callouses on her hands, and a history of shoplifting. She is impulsive and appears a little anxious. client 2 is a 19-year-old female who is underweight, reports losing 18 pounds in the last month, and she is very pale.  A new nurse asks you what the diagnosis is for each of the clients being admitted. You advise that one client is suffering from bulimia and the other is suffering from anorexia.
Which client is suffering from anorexia, and which is suffering from bulimia?
Discuss the presentation of signs/symptoms of both anorexia and bulimia.
Explain at least two nursing interventions for a person with an eating disorder. Include what eating disorder the intervention is appropriate for and why.
Anorexia/Bulimia/Binging

slides.title: A client is being discharged from a 30-day inpatient treatment program for substance misuse. The client asks the nurse for discharge instructions in writing so he can refer to them later. He hands the nurse a list of questions to address.
text: A client is being discharged from a 30-day inpatient treatment program for substance misuse. The client asks the nurse for discharge instructions in writing so he can refer to them later. He hands the nurse a list of questions to address.
Provide answers for each of the following. Include an explanation for each answer.
Now that I have not used drugs for 30 days, I am cured. What should I tell my old friends when we get together this weekend? They are throwing me a welcome home party.
I am having my wisdom teeth removed next week; do I need to tell the oral surgeon about my treatment here?
How many drinks a week can I have where it will not impact my treatment; I am only going to drink beer, so I won’t be drunk or anything.
Do you think I should go to NA or AA meetings? I am not very religious, so I am thinking those are not for me?
Substance Misuse
